title: Competition, Contracts, and Creativity: Evidence from Novel Writing in a Platform Market
eligible_reason: Single-date DiD: romance genres (modern_romance, ancient_romance) vs other genres around one 2014 regulation (NCA) that induced entry into romance; NCA_treat = NCA x treatment switches on at the same calendar month for every treated book. One adoption date, so not staggered. Every column also adds time-varying category-month market controls (cate_month_hits_total, cate_month_subs_total, cate_ebooks_web, cate_nbooks_web); half add category-specific trends and book age; Tables 6 and 8 add contract-type triple interactions.
design_notes: Book-month panel of 1,944 contracted books on a Chinese online-fiction platform, 2013-2015 (Tables.do: areg log_outcome NCA_treat _Iyearmonth* market controls [category trends, age], ab(bookid) cl(category), wild bootstrap boottest). Treatment assigned at the genre level (2 treated vs 3 control genres). Figures 2A-D are model-free treated-minus-control means.
estimators_reported: twfe_static (single treatment date) with time-varying market controls
ineligible_specs_listed: Tables 3A-3B, 7, 8A: NCA_treat with market controls (and category trends/age in even columns); single adoption date
Tables 4, 8B: subsample by contract type, with controls and trends; single date
Tables 6, 8B: triple difference NCA x treatment x share contract
data_files_note: readme.pdf: confidentiality agreement with the platform; dataset.dta / main_dataset.dta not provided (variable dictionary, do-files and logs only).
screener_notes: Not staggered (one regulation date, genre-level assignment); would also fail on controls. No article text; abstract from OpenAlex frame.
